references.text: Wisdom has prepared her meal and sent out her servants to invite the guests: 'Come, eat of my bread' ([ref:Ordsp 9:2-5|Proverbs 9:2-5]). This is a parallel to the servant who is sent out to call those invited to the ready meal.

The preceding verse in the parable of the great banquet, where a man prepares a large meal and invites many ([ref:Luk 14:16|Luke 14:16]). Verse 17 continues with the servant being sent out when everything is ready.

The excuses of those invited follow immediately after the invitation in verse 17 ([ref:Luk 14:18-20|Luke 14:18-20]). Despite everything being prepared and the servant being sent, the invited guests decline the invitation.

Matthew's parallel parable about the king's wedding feast, where the king sends his servants out to call those invited and say that the meal is ready: 'See, I have made my dinner ready' ([ref:Matt 22:2-4|Matthew 22:2-4]). The same motif of servants being sent to those who were already invited.

In Matthew's version, the king says the wedding is ready, but those invited were not worthy ([ref:Matt 22:8|Matthew 22:8]). The same theme that everything has been prepared ('ἕτοιμά ἐστιν') but the guests do not come.

The invitation to the Lamb's marriage supper: 'Blessed are those who are invited to the Lamb's marriage supper' ([ref:Åp 19:9|Revelation 19:9]). The motif of being called/invited (κεκλημένοι) to the heavenly feast.

God's open invitation to come and enjoy his meal: 'Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters ... hear me, so that you may eat what is good' ([ref:Jes 55:1-2|Isaiah 55:1-2]). A parallel to the call 'Come, for everything is ready'.

Jesus laments over Jerusalem which would not accept his invitation: 'How often I wanted to gather your children ... but you were unwilling' ([ref:Luk 13:34|Luke 13:34]). The same theme of rejecting God's repeated invitation.

Paul exhorts: 'See, now is the favorable time; see, now is the day of salvation!' ([ref:2 Kor 6:2|2 Corinthians 6:2]). A parallel to that the 'hour' (τῇ ὥρᾳ) has come and everything is ready—the time of grace is now.
'Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts' ([ref:Hebr 3:7-8|Hebrews 3:7-8]). The same call to respond immediately to God's invitation, without delaying or refusing.
